recommended_subset: The extractor must be a small sequential interpreter, not a pattern matcher, evaluated once per candidate player count (P = 2..8, with cNumberPlayers = P+1, cNumberNonGaiaPlayers = P and their file-local aliases PlayerNum/numPlayer/numPlayers; cNumberTeams and team composition supplied as scenario parameters or enumerated). Minimum it must EVALUATE: (1) flat function-level symbol table with typed declarations (int/float/string/vector) and sequential last-write-wins assignment — including declarations that appear inside an if-branch but remain visible afterwards; (2) constant folding of + - * / with int/float promotion, parentheses, negative and float literals, and string concatenation with numeric coercion (area/grouping names like \"westforest\"+i are identity-bearing); (3) if / else if / else with braced, unbraced-single-statement and empty bodies, conditions using == != < <= > >= && || and bool literals — branching on the folded player-count aliases must select exactly one arm; (4) all three for-loop forms — for(i=1; <N), for(i=1; <= N), and full C-style for(i=0; i<N; i++) — with implicit loop-variable declaration, implicit +1 step in the shorthand forms, break, and postfix ++; loops over player count must be unrolled per P; (5) function calls as statements and as nested argument expressions, with an evaluator for the pure conversion builtins rmXTilesToFraction/rmZTilesToFraction/rmXFractionToMeters/rmZFractionToMeters/rmXMetersToFraction/rmZMetersToFraction/rmAreaTilesToFraction/rmDegreesToRadians — these REQUIRE the current map size, so rmSetMapSize(size,size) and the player-count-branched size variable must be folded first, in program order; (6) opaque-handle modelling: rmCreateArea/rmCreateObjectDef/rmCreateGrouping/rmCreateTradeRoute/rmRiverCreate/rmDefineClass/rmCreate*Constraint return fresh ids bound to variables, and property setters (rmSetAreaSize, rmSetAreaLocation, rmSetObjectDefMin/MaxDistance, rmAddTradeRouteWaypoint, waypoint lists, constraints) accumulate onto the handle with last-write-wins per property (rmSetAreaSize is legitimately called up to 4 times on one area under player-count guards); (7) a tainted-value lattice for vectors and ints: rmGetUnitPosition(rmGetUnitPlacedOfPlayer(...)), rmFindClosestPointVector, rmGetTradeRouteWayPoint, rmPlayerLocXFraction/ZFraction, rmRandInt/rmRandFloat, rmGetNomadStart, rmGetIsKOTH, rmGetPlayerCiv, rmGetPlayerTeam, rmGetNumberPlayersOnTeam, rmAllocateSubCivs, rmGetCivID produce runtime-dependent values; xsVectorGetX/Y/Z and arithmetic/concat propagate the taint, and any geometry argument that ends up tainted is emitted as 'runtime-dependent' with its symbolic expression (e.g. 'xsVectorGetX(pos(pirateControllerID1)) placed at literal (0.17,0.30) => approx resolvable') rather than a guessed number; (8) comment stripping for //, glued // after code, and multi-hundred-line /* */ blocks BEFORE any extraction; (9) tolerant argument parsing: trailing commas in arg lists, multiple statements per physical line, raw backslashes in strings; (10) zpcrownlands' zpGetTeamPlayer helper either inline-executed (its result depends only on rmGetPlayerTeam, so taint it) or treated as a tainted global read of g_zpTeamPlayerResult. xsArrayCreateInt/SetInt/GetInt with constant-foldable indices are trivial to support and appear only in trigger wiring, so implement them cheaply or skip with the trigger sections.
safe_to_skip: Entire trigger DSL blocks: rmCreateTrigger, rmSwitchToTrigger, rmTriggerID, rmAddTriggerCondition, rmAddTriggerEffect, rmSetTriggerConditionParam*/EffectParam*, rmSetTriggerPriority/Active/RunImmediately/Loop — no geometry output; note the for-loops wrapping them still need parsing (parse-and-discard, do not blind-skip lines, because trigger loops share loop variables k/x/s/i with the rest of main)
xsArray create/set/get (used only to shuttle handles into trigger params in these four files)
rmSetStatusText progress-bar calls and rmEchoInfo diagnostics

Commented-out code: // lines and the huge /* */ blocks at the tails of zpkingofbohemia.xs (line 2930 to end) and zpcrownlands.xs (line 1997 to end) plus small /* */ patches around zpkingofbohemia.xs:515-525 — must be stripped, never extracted
seasonPicker in 000_Elbe.xs (declared from rmRandFloat, never consumed) and other dead declarations like evenOdd, classPortSite duplicates
hazards: Variables reassigned between uses: size, numTries, numCliffs, numSockets are set then conditionally overwritten before consumption, and vector socketLoc1/socketLoc2 is reassigned between EVERY rmPlaceObjectDefAtPoint — a regex that pairs a variable with its first assignment produces wrong numbers for all but the first placement

Player-count branching everywhere, on FOUR different spellings of the same value (cNumberNonGaiaPlayers, PlayerNum, numPlayer, numPlayers) plus mixed comparison styles (>=3 ladders vs ==5||==6 vs range &&) — extraction must be evaluated per player count, not collapsed; zpkingofbohemia.xs:52-57 even has a duplicated 'if (cNumberNonGaiaPlayers >= 5)' pair where the second silently overwrites the first (size 460 is dead)

Tile/fraction conversions (rmXTilesToFraction etc.) are NOT constants — they depend on the map size set by the player-count-branched rmSetMapSize earlier in program order; folding them with a fixed map size gives wrong offsets for every non-2-player count

Runtime-only reads that must be flagged 'runtime-dependent', never guessed: rmGetUnitPosition(rmGetUnitPlacedOfPlayer(...)), rmFindClosestPointVector (depends on pushed closest-point constraints AND generated terrain), rmGetTradeRouteWayPoint (interpolates the BUILT route, not the waypoint list), rmPlayerLocXFraction/ZFraction (depends on rmPlacePlayersCircular randomness and teamStartLoc = rmRandFloat), rmRandInt/rmRandFloat, rmGetNomadStart, rmGetIsKOTH, rmGetPlayerTeam/Civ, rmGetNumberPlayersOnTeam-derived spawnType/weirdMap in zpcrownlands (depends on team composition, not just player count)

rmSetAreaSize is called up to four times on the same area handle under player-count guards (riverArea1, centralLake) — semantics are sequential overwrite; a first-match or all-matches regex reports 2700 tiles for an 8-player map instead of 6000

Loop-generated entities: 'westforest'+i, 'eastForest'+i, 'forest '+i, 'edge mountains'+q create up to 80 areas per loop with count depending on player count AND on runtime build failures (break after 5 consecutive rmBuildArea failures) — static extraction can only report the attempted range

Commented-out code is lethal to naive regex: both mod files end with several hundred lines of /* */-wrapped trigger+geometry code, and // lines contain plausible calls like rmSetMapElevationParameters and 'seasonPicker = 0.77' — comment stripping must happen before matching, including // glued directly to code with no space

Function-level (not block) scoping: 'int riverID' declared inside an if-branch is reassigned in the else and used after (000_Elbe.xs:347-353); 'string fish1' likewise in zpcrownlands.xs:83-86 — a block-scoped evaluator loses these variables

Values flow through a mutable global: zpGetTeamPlayer writes g_zpTeamPlayerResult which is snapshotted into fourteen attacker/defender variables that steer placements — treating calls as pure or reading the global once gives wrong player indices

Shorthand loop variables (i, k, x, s, q) are implicitly declared and REUSED across many later loops in the same function; after the forest loop breaks early, 'i' keeps its exit value and leaks into subsequent names like rmCreateObjectDef("berries"+i) — evaluators must carry loop-exit values forward

Syntax tolerance required: trailing comma in arg list rmSetTriggerEffectParamInt("Player2", y,) (zpkingofbohemia.xs), two statements on one physical line with a contradictory duplicate rmSetObjectDefTradeRouteID (000_Elbe.xs:797-798, second call wins), raw backslashes in string literals ("new_england\shoreline3_ne"), and both shorthand and full C-style for-loops in the same file

Waypoint lists are order- and branch-sensitive: trade routes append waypoints inside player-count branches, so the polyline itself differs per player count; extracting waypoints without replaying the branch yields a route that mixes mutually exclusive segments

rmPlaceObjectDefAtLoc coordinates that LOOK literal are sometimes derived: estateW1x..estateE3z are float variables assigned once (safe), but bridgeDock locations are bridgeX+rmXTilesToFraction(22) (map-size dependent) — distinguishing the two requires evaluation, not pattern class
